core.title: Cached or incremental results: plan reuse acceptances and hit-rate measurement
core.given: Work reuses or incrementally recomputes an expensive, repeatable read or derivation with stable identities and tractable dependencies
core.when: writing its acceptance tests or tests
core.then: Include tests for cold and warm paths, staleness, invalidation races, tenant isolation and equivalence with the accepted result, and measure hit rate.
prefer: Equivalence acceptances that compare cached/incremental output with the accepted (uncached) result.
avoid: Treating hit rate as proof of correctness without equivalence and staleness tests.
core.why: Reuse is only trustworthy if tests show warm results equal accepted results, stay fresh and stay isolated.
evidence: Acceptance tests/tests exist for cold/warm paths, staleness, invalidation races, isolation and accepted-result equivalence; hit rate is measured.
verification: Advisory pattern guidance: severity 3, disposition advisory; this rule is not independent enforcement and has no dedicated check of its own.
The stack's existing plan-artifact and source validators still apply.

values: expensive repeatable read or derivation with stable identity and tractable dependencies, planned for reuse or incremental recompute
facts.note: REQUIRED applicability gate: the rule applies only when this finding holds. Same applicability criteria as the reuse-contracts rule. No phase restriction.
OPTIONAL hint only: the presence of these terms does not gate applicability.

fires: Writing acceptance tests or acceptance-carrying plan artifacts, i.e. only the plan-artifact kinds listed in the profile (keys roles.acceptance_test.name and roles.plan_artifact.kinds), for a bounded slice of the product that reuses or incrementally recomputes an expensive, repeatable, stably identified result.
doesNotFire: Results that are not reused or incrementally recomputed.
Work outside the applicability criteria (one-off, cheap, no stable identity, intractable dependencies).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the acceptance-test role and its artifacts; it supplies the local word used for 'acceptance tests' in this rule's 'when' clause and trigger.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds that carry acceptances and are in this rule's trigger scope; the core fires only on these kinds, never on every plan artifact.

neutralityNotes: Three things could not be carried literally. (1) The REQUIRED/OPTIONAL gating semantics of the activation facts live in the Bun sidecar's fact notes; they are now encoded explicitly in the core facts' own notes (REQUIRED applicability gate with no phase restriction; optional task-term hint that does not gate), with the sibling rule referenced by name ('reuse-contracts') rather than by a realization id. (2) The local trigger tokens 'acceptances' and 'DESIRED OUTCOMES' have no neutral wording fixed in advance; they are supplied on instantiation through the existing vocabulary keys roles.acceptance_test.name and roles.plan_artifact.kinds, which also constrains the core trigger to the acceptance-carrying plan-artifact kinds rather than all plan artifacts. (3) 'product capability' is rendered as 'a bounded slice of the product', the gloss the vocabulary itself gives for the product capability layout term. Per the notProfileKeys policy, severity 3 / advisory disposition stays with the rule in core:verification, and the shared-policy id shared:policy.pattern-guidance is bunOnly.
